The corporate takeover of American politics was rapid and ruthless.

In the 1970s, I watched as thousands of corporate lobbyists descended on Washington. Fast forward to today, and lobbying has become a multi-billion dollar industry.

It all began with the Powell Memo.

Video

Billionaire tax cuts are a policy choice.

Cutting healthcare for millions is a policy choice.

Cutting food assistance for children is a policy choice.

Taking from the poor and giving to the rich is a policy choice.

It does not have to be like this.

In another Dem overperformance last night, Democrat Chedrick Greene won by 9 points in a MI Senate seat Kamala Harris barely won.

Dems will retain control of the chamber through 2026.

The midterm momentum is against Trump and the GOP — which is why they're fighting to rig maps.

Independent estimates warn the Iran War has cost $72B so far — nearly triple what Trump's DoD has admitted.

That's over $1 billion per day.

People don't want this. They want a living wage. They want healthcare. They want affordable housing. They want their basic needs met.

50 years ago, the Supreme Court made a consequential ruling on campaign finance reform that doesn't get enough attention today.

But it opened the floodgates to big money spending in our elections — and the corporate takeover of American politics. 

Here's what you should know.

At 40,000 acres, it would be 2.5x the size of Manhattan.

The commission approved the proposal despite opposition from hundreds of locals.

I’ve Argued Before the Supreme Court. Today’s Ruling Shocked Me.

The corporate takeover of American politics was rapid and ruthless.

In the 1970s, I watched as thousands of corporate lobbyists descended on Washington. Fast forward to today, and lobbying has become a multi-billion dollar industry.

It all began with the Powell Memo.

On this day in 1935, FDR signed an executive order creating the Works Progress Administration (WPA). Of 2,000 WPA posters known to exist—publicizing community activities, theatrical productions, and health and educational programs—the Library's collection of more than 900 is the largest.

Remember: NOAA experienced major cuts courtesy of DOGE.

The National Weather Service, which is part of NOAA and provides life saving weather forecasting, was hit hard. 

But now, ahead of storm season, the Trump admin is scrambling to rehire employees that were fired.

"Efficiency."

The billionaire money fighting California’s proposed wealth tax shows how fast extreme wealth translates into outsized political power in this country.

Great piece from the incomparable @rbreich.bsky.social, citing our research on how billionaire political influence has surged post-Citizens United.

You might recognize @benmckenzie.bsky.social from his memorable roles on "The OC" and "Gotham."

In his new documentary, he plays himself: an anti-corruption crusader taking on the lies of the cryptocurrency industry.

Heather and I had the pleasure of chatting with him.

Billionaire tax cuts are a policy choice.

Cutting healthcare for millions is a policy choice.

Cutting food assistance for children is a policy choice.

Taking from the poor and giving to the rich is a policy choice.

It does not have to be like this.

Don't forget: my old Yale Law classmate Clarence Thomas refused to recuse from Jan. 6 cases despite his wife's involvement in the plot.

And he's taken at least 100 gifts worth over $2 million while serving, including from GOP donor Harlan Crow.

He's a disgrace to the Court.

Airline ticket prices are surging.

A major culprit? Rising jet fuel costs due to Trump's Iran war.

But there's also the underlying concentration in the industry.

Airlines merged from 12 major carriers in 1980 to 4 today.

Less competition makes it easier for the biggest players to price-gouge.

Big Oil is making a $30 million windfall profit every HOUR by using the Iran War as an excuse to rip off commuters at the gas pump.

This year, Exxon will be spending $20 billion of its profits on stock buybacks.

We must end the Iran War and pass a windfall profits tax — NOW!

Big day—the NYT published an opinion piece arguing that moving to the center might not work  

www.nytimes.com/2026/05/05/o...

Look I'm no political strategist but it seems to me that when the President's chief financial advisor is going around gleefully talking about how great it is that everyone's spending more on things and that credit card spending is up, that would be useful for opposition political messaging...

If you saw this happening in another country, what would you call it?

CEO pay rose 20 times faster than worker pay in 2025, per Oxfam.

Overall, global worker pay declined 12% between 2019 and 2025 — while CEO pay rose 54% during the same time.

Trickle-down economics was always a sham. www.theguardian.com/business/202...

I've spent a lifetime teaching young people — and I wouldn't trade it for anything in the world.

These are the most important lessons I've learned along the way. www.youtube.com/watch?v=fpjs...

Ag Secretary Brooke Rollins cheered on 4.3 million Americans losing SNAP benefits thanks to Trump's Big Ugly Bill.

That's the biggest drop in food assistance in nearly 30 years — all to give the ultra-rich even more tax cuts.

A gallon of gas is now 50% more expensive than when Trump started his Iran War. In the war's first month, the 100 biggest oil and gas companies brought in an extra $30 million per HOUR in windfall profits. Trump's Big Oil donors come out on top while the world suffers.
This week is Teacher Appreciation Week. Let me tell you about one teacher in particular who changed my life forever. Mrs. Alice Camp.
The greatest honor of my life wasn't serving in the Cabinet. It was being a teacher.
I've spent a lifetime teaching young people — and I wouldn't trade it for anything in the world. These are the most important lessons I've learned along the way.
Trump's tariffs and war with Iran are costing the American people more every day. In November, the GOP will pay the price.
Why is the President of the United States shilling so hard for cryptocurrency? Because the entire industry is a Ponzi scheme — and he's the conman-in-chief.

The Supreme Court gutted the Voting Rights Act of 1965 this week. It was a slap in the face to the countless activists who fought for the VRA — and those who died for it. But we cannot give up. Here's how we should respond.
You've probably heard a lot about general strikes. But how exactly do they work? And is America on the verge of one? Labor journalist Kim Kelly explains.
The decision made today by the Supreme Court’s conservative majority was dishonest and shameful. I want to share some thoughts on what it means — and how we move forward.

A Supreme Court so fundamentally hostile to the rights of minority voters places the Court at odds with democracy itself. This is the legacy of Chief Justice John Roberts. I opposed his nomination back in 2005, and I stand by that.
An actual king understands democracy better than Trump.
